chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Hasan al-Attar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'borrowing of the private part' (temporary marriage for a specific purpose), and he said: 'There is no harm in it.' I said: 'But if a child is born from it?' He said: 'It belongs to the owner of the girl, unless he stipulates otherwise upon him.'

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْجَارِيَةِ: The owner of the girl (referring to the woman in the contract)
key_terms.عَارِيَّةِ الْفَرْجِ: Borrowing of the private part (a form of temporary marriage)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَ: He stipulates (a condition in the contract)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits or owns the child from temporary marriage (I'radat al-Farj) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the jurisprudential ruling on 'I'radat al-Farj' (temporary marriage for the purpose of facilitating a woman's remarriage), specifically addressing the lineage of offspring. It establishes the default principle that the child belongs to the woman's husband (the 'owner of the girl') unless the man explicitly stipulates otherwise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contractual clarity in determining nasab (lineage) within temporary unions.
